item.description:
Says that ⌥ is there

Force quitting is the one thing here you would never stumble upon — nobody holds a modifier over a thumbnail to see what happens. The welcome panel now mentions it alongside the other shortcuts.

Force quit, and steadier around apps that hang

  • Hold ⌥ over a thumbnail and the red button turns black. One click quits that application outright — for the window with no close button, the close button that does nothing, and the app that stopped answering some time ago.
  • Windows offering no controls at all used to get no badge, which left them beyond reach entirely. Holding ⌥ now reaches them.
  • An unresponsive app no longer slows everything down. Asking it questions used to block for seconds at a time, and the badge stopped appearing over every other window as well. It gives up quickly now and does not keep asking.

First release

Window controls that work, drawn over Mission Control’s thumbnails: close, minimize and zoom whichever window you are pointing at, without leaving the overview.

  • The buttons follow your cursor from thumbnail to thumbnail, sized and placed to match the window underneath.
  • ⌘W, ⌘M and ⌃⌘F act on the window you are pointing at, and ⌘Q quits the app behind it.
  • Arrow keys walk the grid, Return brings a window to the front.
  • Works the same in App Exposé, across several displays and Spaces.
